threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the TfL app before hopping on the bus—locals know half the time it’s quicker to just walk.
Caught a night bus from Brixton; two drummers arguing about rhythms turned into a spontaneous jam session. Whole bus was vibing!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a full suit chatting with a busker while waiting for the tram—only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you enjoy a late-night döner with live saxophone on the corner—just another Wednesday vibe that feels so uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their quiet disdain for tourists trying to take photos in front of the taco trucks at midnight. Total vibe killer.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing the harp on the 31-Balboa, totally drowned out by the bus's screeching brakes. Classic Muni moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think all the bars here close at 2 AM, but locals know it’s not uncommon to find a few hidden spots open well into the sunrise.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still reference 'el metro' when everyone just says 'el metro' without the article. Little things like that give them away.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Dalston Junction' instead of just 'The Junction.' Everyone knows it's just Dalston now—welcome to the club.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham and overheard a couple arguing about who left the pizza slice out. Classic South London drama.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in lederhosen juggling apples in Hermannplatz while a street musician played accordion—definitely a Neukölln day.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip on a coffee while watching a spontaneous dance-off in the U-Bahn station—so quintessentially Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate the BART delays; they know to grab a burrito before heading to the station, just in case.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 Mission at the right time today. A guy serenading us with an old guitar—other riders just vibing. Muni can surprise you sometimes.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume all Gràcia's squares are for lounging, but locals know that by sundown, plaça de la Virreina transforms into a lively performance stage.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their shyness when asking for directions at the metro station—locals just dive in confidently.
